(1) AGN are just scaled-up versions of Galactic black holes; (2) the characteristic X-ray variability time scale of AGN is physically linked to their mass and accretion rate; (3) this time scale is the same as that found for Galactic black holes; and (4) the optical permitted emission line widths are a direct measure of the black hole mass and accret ion rate.

(i) the X-ray timescale is the same for AGN and Galactic systems, (ii) the X-ray variations are driven by changes in the accreted mass rate, (iii) the accretion flow is the same for both types of system, (iv) the optical emission lines are driven by changes to the accretion, and (v) the optical emission-line widths are determined by the mass of the central black hole.
